note: restock() calls contains_key(item) and then get_mut(item) on the same key (insert on the miss path), so the key is hashed twice where entry(item).or_insert(0) would do it once.
roster.get(&id) and by_student.entry(...) are lookups in two different maps, and the grouping map is updated once per score through the entry API.
leg_minutes() looks up two different keys (from and to) once each, so there is no repeated lookup of the same key.

Settings::resolve() checks overrides.contains_key(key) and then indexes overrides[key] for the same key, where a single overrides.get(key) would do; the defaults lookup is a different map and does not count.
Warehouse::reserve() does stock.get(&sku) and then stock.insert(sku, available - qty) for the same key, where one get_mut would update the count in place; release_all() already uses the entry API.
Adjacency lists are built with entry(a)/entry(b) on different keys, BFS uses one links.get per town and HashSet::insert's return value, so no key is looked up twice.
check() consults the banned HashSet and then the buckets map (different collections), and the bucket itself is fetched once via entry().or_insert and mutated in place.
Bus::subscribe() does contains_key(&topic), then insert, then get_mut(&topic).unwrap() on the same key, i.e. a hand-rolled entry(topic).or_default().push(handler) with up to three lookups.
The order book uses first_entry/last_entry to get and remove the best level in one search, entry().or_default() to rest orders, and one get per depth query; bids and asks are separate maps.
Index::add_total() does totals.get(term) and then totals.insert(term, updated) for the same key, where entry(term).or_insert(0) += n would search once; the other map updates use entry.
